A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrowdNotes+ and HealthNotes. All 13 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable; the text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original analysis of 30,791 health-related notes, experiments with 15 LLMs on HealthNotes, ablations, evidence comparisons, and human-reviewed error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds human assessments of the relevance and correctness judges in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: The two generation modes, diverse-query retrieval, iterative utility selection, passage matching, and sequential evaluation gates are retained. Generation prompts and HealthJudge training remain substantively unchanged; additional workflow documentation does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English health domain, 30,791-note observational corpus, and balanced 1,268-example HealthNotes benchmark. The new judge checks and workflow examples remain within this coverage; no additional benchmark, language, or deployment scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The human baseline and 15 evaluated LLM configurations are retained in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. The HealthJudge comparison, ablation variants, and o3/MedGemma-27B evidence comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix E.4 introduces a human verification protocol: 100 judgments per relevance/correctness stage, balanced across the two benchmark subsets, independently assessed by three graduate students and aggregated by majority vote. Existing benchmark splits, retrieval controls, model configurations, and length constraints remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct human reliability checks for both upstream evaluation judges, substantially extending validation beyond the retained HealthJudge comparison and error analyses. Appendix G also adds two complete workflow cases. The earlier query-diversity and utility ablations, evidence-preference analyses, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.2 newly states that all experiments were run once; v1 disclosed temperature settings but no run count. This is disclosure, not evidence of changed repetition. Appendix E.4 also introduces judge–human agreement and inter-annotator disagreement reporting, without confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched latency, benchmark, ablation, evidence-utility, and HealthJudge table values are unchanged. New results include agreement with human verification in 100/100 relevance cases and 97/100 correctness cases, plus the generated notes and passing evaluation outcomes in Figures 10–11.

T1.justification: Equation (1) replaces P(H(n)=1) on the left-hand side with the joint probability P(R=1,C=1,H=1), explicitly making the factorization describe satisfaction of all three criteria. This is a limited formal correction; the sequential procedure is unchanged and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the two-mode CrowdNotes+ framework, hierarchical evaluation, HealthNotes with HealthJudge, and findings about crowd-rating weaknesses and LLM assistance. The rewritten abstract and conclusion emphasize these retained claims without establishing a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands deployment qualifications beyond v1's general human-oversight statement. Its Ethical Considerations discuss hallucination, automation bias, citation-backed disinformation, and English-source bias, explicitly discourage autonomous health governance, and require human evidence verification. Existing language, domain, and retrieval limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit retriever-to-generator mapping in Table 7, identifies the source-categorization judge in Appendix B.1, and supplies human annotation instructions in Appendix E.4. Existing APIs, passage sizes, embeddings, training hyperparameters, and model versions are retained; most technical material is relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xing et al.'s CommunityNotes dataset citation and removes Augenstein et al.'s community-moderation reference. Related work places greater emphasis on preserving human control, and the introduction explicitly credits earlier latency findings by Renault et al.; the overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The four-question experimental narrative becomes separate Experiments and three-question Discussions sections, while deployment discussion and technical material are reorganized into Appendices A–G. Limitations and Ethical Considerations become separate sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, typography, margins, caption placement, and display arrangement throughout. Figure 3 is revised, existing tables and figures are reformatted or relocated, and Table 7 plus workflow Figures 10–11 are added. Most original plots retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The new human judge checks strengthen support for the evaluation pipeline, while the corrected probability expression, explicit retriever mapping, and substantive deployment qualifications improve precision and transparency. The gains are bounded: the checks assess displayed judge reasoning on sampled cases, and the central experiments and findings remain unchanged.
